docs.title: Reservoir History Matching
docs.text: Assisted history matching with production data assimilation and forecasting.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This machine learning system is part of the Oil & Gas ML Portfolio by Kelvin J Cabrera.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Synthetic Data Generator -> Scikit-Learn Training -> Flask API -> Streamlit Dashboard

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Data Generation: Domain-aware synthetic data with physical correlations
  • Model Training: Scikit-learn pipelines (Random Forest, Isolation Forest) with MLflow tracking
  • API: Flask/FastAPI with API key authentication
  • Dashboard: Streamlit interactive web interface
  • Testing: pytest with model evaluation metrics (R2, accuracy, F1)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements.txt
python train.py
python app.py
streamlit run streamlit_app.py

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Endpoint Description GET / Service info and available models POST /predict/{model} Run inference (requires API key)

Authentication

All API endpoints require an X-API-Key header. Set API_KEY in your environment.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All API requests require an API key sent via the X-API-Key header.

import requests

headers = {"X-API-Key": "your-api-key"}
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5000/predict/model", json={...}, headers=headers)

docs.title: GET /
docs.text:
Returns service information and available models.

Response:

{"service": "Reservoir History Matching", "models": ["model1", "model2"]}

docs.title: POST /predict/{model_name}
docs.text:
Run inference on a trained model.

Request Body:

{"features": {"feature_1": 0.5, "feature_2": 1.2}}

Response:

{"prediction": 0.85, "model": "model_name"}

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text: Code Description 401 Invalid or missing API key 404 Model not found 422 Invalid input format

docs.title: Data Layer
docs.text:
• Data Source: Synthetic reservoir data generator (ReservoirDataGenerator) producing 50 wells with 100 timesteps each
  • Well Properties: Porosity, permeability, depth, water saturation, net pay, pressure, temperature, viscosity
  • Production Data: Oil rate, water rate, gas rate per timestep
  • Preprocessing: Standard scaling with persistent preprocessor (pickle serialized)

docs.title: History Matcher
docs.text:
• Algorithm: GradientBoosting regressor
  • Input: 8 reservoir properties (porosity, permeability, depth, water_saturation, net_pay, pressure, temperature, viscosity)
  • Output: 3 production rates (oil_rate_bopd, water_rate_bwpd, gas_rate_mscfd)
  • Metrics: R2, MAE, RMSE (train/test splits)
  • Purpose: Map static reservoir properties to production performance

docs.title: Production Forecaster
docs.text:
• Algorithm: GradientBoosting with sliding window approach
  • Input: Lookback window of recent production data (default: 10 timesteps)
  • Output: Future production rates for n_steps ahead
  • Metrics: R2, MAE, RMSE (train/test splits)
  • Purpose: Forecast future production from historical trends (alternative to LSTM/RNN)

docs.title: API Layer
docs.text:
• Framework: Flask
  • Endpoints: 5 REST endpoints (health, models, predict, forecast, docs)
  • Model Loading: Eager loading at startup from outputs/models/
  • Persistence: Preprocessor saved as pickle for consistent transformations

docs.title: Dashboard Layer
docs.text:
• Frontend: Flask + HTML/CSS/JS
  • Features: Reservoir property input, production prediction, forecast visualization

docs.title: History Matching Flow
docs.text:
1. Input: 8 reservoir properties as numeric array
  2. Preprocessing: ReservoirPreprocessor applies standard scaling
  3. Prediction: HistoryMatcher predicts 3 production rates simultaneously
  4. Response: Oil, water, and gas rates in standard units

docs.title: Forecasting Flow
docs.text:
1. Input: Recent production history (array of records) + n_steps
  2. Preprocessing: Format into lookback windows
  3. Prediction: ProductionForecaster generates multi-step forecasts
  4. Response: Array of predicted production rates for each future timestep

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Generate synthetic reservoir data (50 wells, 100 timesteps)
  2. Generate history matching dataset (properties -> rates)
  3. Train HistoryMatcher with 80/20 split
  4. Generate forecast dataset with lookback windows
  5. Train ProductionForecaster with 80/20 split
  6. Save models and preprocessor to outputs/models/
  7. Print metrics for both models

docs.text:

├── reservoir_history_matching/

docs.title: Dockerfile
docs.text:
FROM python:3.10-slim

WORKDIR /app

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

RUN python train.py

EXPOSE 5006

CMD ["python", "app.py"]

docs.title: Build and Run
docs.text:
docker build -t reservoir-history-matching .
docker run -p 5006:5006 reservoir-history-matching

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
version: '3.8'
services:
  app:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "5006:5006"
    environment:
      - FLASK_DEBUG=0
    volumes:
      - ./outputs:/app/outputs
    restart: unless-stopped

docker-compose up -d

docs.text: Variable Description Default FLASK_DEBUG Enable debug mode 1 PORT Server port 5006 HOST Server host 0.0.0.0

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Set DEBUG=False in production
  • Use HTTPS with a reverse proxy
  • Add authentication for prediction endpoints
  • Validate input feature ranges

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text:
• Monitor /api/health for model availability
  • Track prediction accuracy over time
  • Monitor forecast drift from actuals
  • Log all API requests

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• Models loaded eagerly at startup
  • Consider model versioning for A/B testing
  • Use feature caching for repeated reservoir properties

docs.title: Model Management
docs.text:
• Retrain periodically with new production data
  • Compare model versions using metrics from /api/models
  • Store prediction history for model validation

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: ML-based reservoir production history matching and forecasting system. Uses GradientBoosting to match reservoir properties to production rates and forecast future production from historical data.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8+
  • pip

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/kcabrera83/reservoir-history-matching.git
cd reservoir-history-matching
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Training Models
docs.text:
python train.py

Generates synthetic reservoir data (50 wells, 100 timesteps), trains history matcher and production forecaster.

docs.title: Starting the Server
docs.text:
python app.py

Open http://localhost:5006 in your browser.

docs.title: Dashboard Features
docs.text:
• History Matching: Predict production rates from reservoir properties
  • Production Forecasting: Forecast future production from historical data
  • Model Metrics: View training and testing performance
  • Visualization: Production curves and forecast plots

docs.title: Input Features (for /api/predict)
docs.text: Index Feature Unit Description 0 porosity fraction Rock porosity (0-1) 1 permeability_md mD Rock permeability 2 depth_m m Reservoir depth 3 water_saturation fraction Water saturation (0-1) 4 net_pay_m m Net productive thickness 5 pressure_psi psi Reservoir pressure 6 temperature_c C Reservoir temperature 7 oil_viscosity_cp cP Oil viscosity

docs.title: Output Production Rates
docs.text: Field Unit Description oil_rate_bopd bopd Oil production rate (barrels oil per day) water_rate_bwpd bwpd Water production rate (barrels water per day) gas_rate_mscfd mscfd Gas production rate (thousand standard cubic feet per day)

docs.title: Using curl
docs.text:
# Predict production from reservoir properties
curl -X POST http://localhost:5006/api/predict \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"features": [0.20, 500, 3500, 0.30, 100, 3000, 100, 0]}'

# Forecast future production
curl -X POST http://localhost:5006/api/forecast \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "recent_data": [
      {"oil_rate_bopd": 350, "water_rate_bwpd": 120, "gas_rate_mscfd": 850},
      {"oil_rate_bopd": 345, "water_rate_bwpd": 125, "gas_rate_mscfd": 840}
    ],
    "n_steps": 10
  }'

# Get model information
curl http://localhost:5006/api/models

# Health check
curl http://localhost:5006/api/health

docs.title: Using Python
docs.text:
import requests

# Predict production rates
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5006/api/predict", json={
    "features": [0.20, 500, 3500, 0.30, 100, 3000, 100, 0]
})
prediction = response.json()["prediction"]
print(f"Oil: {prediction['oil_rate_bopd']} bopd")
print(f"Water: {prediction['water_rate_bwpd']} bwpd")
print(f"Gas: {prediction['gas_rate_mscfd']} mscfd")

# Forecast future production
historical_data = [
    {"oil_rate_bopd": 350, "water_rate_bwpd": 120, "gas_rate_mscfd": 850},
    {"oil_rate_bopd": 345, "water_rate_bwpd": 125, "gas_rate_mscfd": 840},
]
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5006/api/forecast", json={
    "recent_data": historical_data,
    "n_steps": 10
})
forecast = response.json()["forecast"]
for step in forecast:
    print(f"Oil: {step['oil_rate_bopd']:.1f} bopd")

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
• History Matcher: GradientBoosting regressor mapping reservoir properties to production rates
  • Production Forecaster: GradientBoosting-based forecaster using lookback windows (alternative to LSTM)

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
The training pipeline follows these steps:

  1. Data Generation: data_generator.py creates synthetic data with domain-specific physical correlations
  2. Preprocessing: Feature scaling via StandardScaler
  3. Training: Random Forest or Isolation Forest via scikit-learn
  4. Evaluation: R2 score, accuracy, classification report
  5. Logging: MLflow tracks parameters, metrics, and artifacts
  6. Serialization: Model + scaler + metadata saved as .pkl via joblib

docs.title: Model Files
docs.text:
Models are stored in outputs/models/*.pkl as dictionaries with:

Key Description model Trained scikit-learn estimator scaler Fitted StandardScaler feature_names List of input feature names target_name Target variable name metrics Evaluation metrics from training

docs.title: Retraining
docs.text:
To retrain:

python train.py

This will update the model files in outputs/models/ and log results to MLflow.
